title: Peira bed config
description: The only place Peira learns about a service (RFC 0001 §4, RFC 0002). Top level is permissive on purpose — peira init writes a $comment, and existing beds must keep working. Principal shapes under `users` are checked strictly in src/validate-bed.ts, because this validator cannot express per-value schemas.

baseUrl.description: Where the service answers. --base-url overrides per invocation.

users.description: Named principals — cases say $users.<alias>, never credentials. Each alias is exactly one shape: Basic {username, password}; login {login: {method?, route, body?, token, send}} — logs in once per run on first use (once even under --parallel), captures the token at a path like body.token, attaches it per send; or static {token, send} for API keys. send is {header, format containing {{token}}} or {cookie}. A refused login makes every case on that principal an error, never a fail. Tokens and passwords are scrubbed from the evidence log by value.

url.description: Route of the service's own wipe-state endpoint.

method.description: HTTP method for the reset call; default post.

reset.description: One wipe-state call before each run, pointed at the service's own endpoint. When the service has no such endpoint, chain a script in service.command instead ("./reset.sh && npm start").

route.description: Route that reports an async job's state.

idParam.description: Query parameter that carries the job id.

statusPath.description: Dotted response path where the state lives, e.g. body.status.

terminal.description: States that mean the job has settled.

drain.description: How to ask the service whether an async job settled: which route, which id parameter, where the state lives in the response, which states are terminal. Powers teardown.drain.

stepMs.description: Ceiling for a registry step's child process.

timeouts.description: Latency-envelope ceilings for a slow environment: {requestMs?, pollUntilMs?, drainMs?, stepMs?}. Hitting one is an error, never a fail. The poll interval stays pinned (determinism).

command.description: Shell command that starts the service. Runs in service.cwd.

readyMs.description: How long to wait for baseUrl to answer (any HTTP response counts) before giving up.

reuse.description: Default true: an already-answering baseUrl is used as-is. false refuses to test an instance Peira did not start (CI).

service.description: How `peira run` starts the app under test: {command, cwd?, readyMs?, reuse?}. The command runs in a shell, so `prep && server` works. reuse (default true) adopts an already-answering baseUrl and never kills it; a server Peira started is killed — whole process group — when the run ends. Only run manages processes.

header.description: Header name, e.g. Authorization or X-API-Key.

format.description: Header value template; must contain {{token}}, e.g. "Bearer {{token}}".

send.description: How a token is attached to every request as this principal: exactly one of the two forms.

password.description: Basic-auth password. Never appears in cases or in the evidence log.

basicPrincipal.description: HTTP Basic: sends Authorization: Basic base64(username:password).

body.description: JSON body of the login request (the credentials). May not reference unique.* — a login belongs to a principal, not a case.

token.description: Capture path into the login response, e.g. body.token or headers.x-session. The value is scrubbed from the evidence log.

send.description: How to attach the captured token to every request.

login.description: The login request and what to do with its response.

loginPrincipal.description: Logs in once per run on first use (once even under --parallel), captures the token, attaches it per send. A refused login makes every case on this principal an error, never a fail.

staticPrincipal.description: A fixed token with no login step — API keys. The value is scrubbed from the evidence log.
